newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pengab bank sector climate warms in March.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pengab bank sector climate warms in March.

text.p: Poland's banking climate index "Pengab" rose 6.4 points to 49.8 in March from 43.4 in February and was 6.6 points higher than in March 1996, a poll released on Tuesday by the private Pentor institute showed.
The monthly survey showed the index grew due to an increase of deposits in both zlotys and foreign currencies as well as an increase of interest in foreign currency denominated credit.
Pentor director Eugeniusz Smilowski told a news conference that the index was in a horisontal trend but that it would likely rise again in April.

He said that banks did not give any indication that they planned to raise credit rates or lower deposit rates further after the central bank increased obligatory reserves on call and currency deposits starting on February 28.
Several commercial banks have adjusted rates after the central bank anounced the move, but most left them flat.
The index, based on a scale of minus 100 to plus 100, polled 204 bank managers and is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
